facts.text: Hartland was first settled around 1800 and incorporated as Warrentown on February 17, 1820, just weeks before Maine became a state.
The town’s public library began in 1903 inside the town hall, moved to Commercial Street in 1935, and settled in its current location in 1991.
In 1995 a tannery donation added a community room and children’s materials to the library, expanding its role in Hartland.
The Hartland Historical Society, founded in 2001, preserves the town’s history through volunteer‑led collections of photos, maps, and artifacts.
A 10‑room house built in 1904 on Main Street remains one of Hartland’s most recognizable historic properties, reflecting early 20th‑century architecture.
The town’s library houses more than 35,000 books and seven computers, offering free access to residents and visitors alike.
